# Solution Design: Action Redirect Views
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent)

Next action: verify the implemented design against the acceptance matrix in Measure.

## Evidence and hypothesis

For issue #68 (bug: every Q&A action also logs a session_viewed (redirect back to the session page)), `SessionQnaController` returns `back()` for every Q&A write and vote, and validation redirects too. The session show GET records `session_viewed` for each non-prefetch request. `AdminCalendarEventController::redirectTo()` sends calendar edits back to `calendar`; `CalendarController` records `calendar_viewed` on that GET. The current `UserActivityTest` asserts Q&A action rows without following the redirect. The UI calls `useForm` and `router.post` with `preserveScroll`, not `only`; installed Inertia builds partial headers only when `only` is set. Thus neither request type nor partial-data headers can reliably distinguish an action refresh from genuine navigation. Hypothesis: following either action redirect produces the extra view row; a feature test must reproduce both.

## Smallest design

Add a route-scoped middleware for Q&A and administrator calendar mutations. When their response is a same-app redirect to a session detail or calendar page, flash the exact redirect URL into the server session for one following request. On a matching GET, consume that flash value in the session/calendar view handler and skip only its view event. The marker is server-generated, URL-scoped, and one-use: a direct navigation or unrelated redirect remains loggable. The action event and rendered Inertia response are unchanged. Ensure validation-error redirects also pass through the middleware and receive the same marker; test this before relying on it. Never accept a query parameter from the browser as an audit bypass. Do not add an activity table column or change historical rows.

The existing prefetch fix in PR #73 (fix: honor Inertia prefetch header for activity views) for issue #69 (bug: activity-log prefetch guard checks X-Inertia-Prefetch, but Inertia sends Purpose: prefetch) remains separate. Keep the current view guard intact and add the action-refresh exclusion alongside it.

## Source and tests

- Route/action seam: `application/source/routes/web.php` and a small server-side middleware/support concern for action redirects. Use `auth`, `active`, and existing `admin` middleware as-is; no new public route.
- View seam: `LearningSessionController::show` and `CalendarController::__invoke` read the one-shot server marker after their existing access/validation checks.
- Tests: `application/source/tests/Feature/UserActivityTest.php` follows successful and failed Q&A redirects, checks action rows and no duplicate views, follows an admin calendar edit redirect, and checks a genuine visit still adds one view. Use synthetic users and records only.
- Operations: update `application/ops/activity-logging.md` to describe the exclusion without implying false historical rows were deleted.
- Evidence: safe synthetic activity-log screenshot in this run at `evidence/activity-log-redirect-exclusion.png`, visually reviewed before publication.

Rollback is a revert of the bounded application changes. Authentication, role checks, private files, video behavior, schema, and data retention are unchanged. Staging and production acceptance remain separate.
